messages:
Maria K: Quick heads-up — running into a parity bug between sync and async in the Python SDK for embeddings.rerank. Sync call returns a dict-like response with 'scores' and 'items', async call yields a tuple (scores, items) and typing says Sequence[float]. Broke our sample-app ordering tests.

Liam C: ugh. Can you paste a minimal repro?

Maria K: repro below (very small):
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()  # v0.9.3
# sync
resp = client.embeddings.rerank(["how to x"], ["doc a", "doc b"])\nprint(type(resp), resp.keys())\n# async
import asyncio\nasync def main():\n    r = await client.embeddings.rerank_async(["how to x"], ["doc a", "doc b"])\n    print(type(r))\nasyncio.run(main())
```
Sync prints <class 'dict'> with keys('scores','items'), async prints <class 'tuple'> and items are numpy arrays.

Samir: I can repro. Looks like the async batching helper (_async_batcher) returns raw kernel outputs and we forgot to run _normalize_response path that the sync flow uses. Also find a preserve_order flag difference — sync defaults preserve_order=True, async was accidentally False in the batching helper, so ordering differs too.

Anika: also saw weirdness with auth/retry: when we hit a transient 401 the async wrapper retries but yields partial streamed results back as a generator object instead of raising, so types diverge again. Might be two separate bugs but they interact in sample-app.

Liam C: breaking down tasks: (1) normalize response path for async to match sync (2) ensure preserve_order default parity (3) add typing hints consistent across both sync and async signatures (no numpy in public API) (4) unit tests for ordering + type in the sample-app CI.

Maria K: workaround for now in sample-app: coerce tuple->dict and cast arrays to lists:
```python
if isinstance(r, tuple):\n    scores, items = r\n    scores = list(scores)\n    items = [list(i) if hasattr(i, 'tolist') else i for i in items]\n    resp = {"scores": scores, "items": items}\nelse:\n    resp = r
```
Not ideal but unblocks testing.

Samir: I'll take the fix. Found a small patch: run normalize in async path and set preserve_order=True in async batcher. Also changed annotations to Sequence[float] and convert numpy to list before returning. Will open PR.

Liam C: thanks. Please include a changelog note (BREAKING? maybe not if we normalize types) and add a short migration note for anyone relying on tuple return.

sdk-bot: PR #3245 created by Samir: fix(async-embed): parity for rerank response shape, enforce preserve_order, normalize numpy -> list. Link: https://git.redwood.dev/r/redwood/sdk/pull/3245

Anika: can someone add a small integration test against sample-app to catch this on CI?

Samir: will add tests and a small sample-app CI job. planning to merge tomorrow unless objections. :thumbsup:

Maria K: thanks all — will remove workaround once PR lands and rerun our onboarding tests.
